note: Informational record of the bug CATEGORIES the hidden oracle (oracle_test.ts, written transiently by grader.py) checks for. The builder writes computeOracleAuditPlan() from scratch -- nothing is literally injected into its code. 'Seeded' here means 'plausible implementation mistakes a cheap builder model might make against this exact spec', which is what the oracle is designed to catch independent of whatever the spec-writer's own acceptance tests happened to cover.

bugs.description: Uses allStates.length (the full, unfiltered input) instead of eligibleAyahIds.length (the filtered mastered-pool size) to decide between sample size 5 and 10 -- gives the wrong base whenever ineligible entries are present.
Uses eligibleAyahIds.length > 50 (strictly greater) instead of >= 50 for the 5-vs-10 threshold, miscategorizing a pool of exactly 50 as sample size 5 instead of 10.
Uses AND instead of OR between the retrievability and intervalDays conditions, wrongly excluding entries that satisfy only one of the two (e.g. interval_days=90 but retrievability=0.80).
Uses intervalDays >= 60 (inclusive) instead of the spec's strict intervalDays > 60, wrongly including an entry at exactly 60 days as eligible via the interval condition.
Returns the raw base sample size (5 or 10) even when eligibleAyahIds.length is smaller than that (e.g. 2 eligible entries, sampleSize should be 2 but returns 5).
Filters or sorts allStates via an in-place method (e.g. .sort() before scanning, or .splice() to remove ineligible entries) instead of leaving the caller's array untouched.
